chapter: Chicago and New York with Louis Armstrong, 1925-30
title: Louis and Earl Hines at the Warwick Hall; leaving Noone for Dickerson
summary: Zutty tells of the short Warwick Hall venture with Louis and Hines, and of leaving Jimmy Noone and the Apex to join Carroll Dickerson at the Savoy.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Well he says, he got, with Dave Peyton at Café de Paris April 27 with Jimmy Noon at the (Nes?) before joining Clarence Jones at the Metropolitan Theater with Louis Armstrong. Left in late '27 playing briefly at the Warwick Hall with Louis Armstrong and Earl (Also Hines?).
Right. But we had been in we were, the Savoy just had opened and we thought we could (bump?) the Savoy because we had Louis and (Father Hines?). And man, nothing happened.
And Clarence Black had the (booking?).
Clarence Black had the band.
Had the band in the Savoy.
In the Savoy.
And you were in that band?
No I wasn't in that band.
Oh, well whose band were you in at the Savoy?
Carroll Dickerson's band.
Oh, Carroll Dickerson.

That's when Louis and I, that's when I left Jimmy Noon at the (Nest?), I mean at the Apex. Because I was subbing for Ollie Powells. He was a drummer and singer in that group with Father Hines and Joe Paston and Bud Scott.
Yes I see, that was after it became the Apex, after the (Nest?) became the Apex.

That's right. But I found out that Louis was going to go ahead with Carroll Dickerson's band because it was rumored all around, you know. At the Savoy and I had to leave Jimmy Noon. I hated to leave him because I liked his band and I liked the way Father Hines played you know. And that's when we opened at the Savoy.
Did Earl leave to go with Carroll Dickerson then?
No.
No he did, he stayed?
Earl had been with Carroll Dickerson before that.
Oh, it was before you were with Carroll then?
Yes. Yes, because that's when
going back to Roulette, that's when Father played for a while at Jeffrey Tavern.
Oh he was in that band?
Oh yes, he was in that band. Didn't stay long because he was just beginning to form his band, see for the Grand Terrace.
